household.title: tobacco-pipe
household.reason: A carved clay pipe bowl in the form of a face with a carved wooden stem, a well-known Cameroon Grassfields form; museum attributes it to Tikar ("perhaps") with no contrary evidence.

masks-ritual.name: Mask
masks-ritual.title: Helmet crest from a Ngumba/Kwifon masquerade
masks-ritual.reason: This is a carved wooden helmet crest with radiating sunburst headdress, used in Kwifon masquerade — the museum attributes it to the Kom peoples, part of the Tikar group, consistent with the claim.

masks-ritual.name: mask
masks-ritual.title: mask
masks-ritual.reason: The image shows a cast brass mask with beard, prominent eyes, and headdress decoration — a Cameroon Grassfields cire-perdue brass mask, the type the cited literature explicitly attributes to the Tikar ("Masque en cuivre. Tribu Tikar (Cameroun)... masque prophylactique"), used as a protective object in wealthy households.
